has spent 2026 warning that AI is moving faster than anyone is ready for.
Now one of its co-founders says the moment has a name.

Jack Clark just said that the singularity, when AI-driven progress starts
outrunning humanity’s ability to keep up, is officially underway. What
comes with it? A possible $44T U.S. economy, serious job disruption, and a
short window to decide if AI needs an intelligence cap.

*LATEST DEVELOPMENTS*

ANTHROPIC
🌌 *Anthropic co-founder says the singularity is underway
*

Image source: IMF

*The Rundown: *Anthropic co-founder Jack Clark just told

economists and policymakers at the IMF and World Bank’s annual meetings
that the singularity, the point where AI speeds up discovery faster than
humans can follow, has “now begun.”

*The details: *

   -

   Clark pointed to AI’s scores on Humanity’s Last Exam (expert-level
   questions) going from 8% to 67.7% since 2025, and FrontierMath improving
   from 2% to 94%.
   -

   One Anthropic model has U.S. GDP at $44T by 2030 if AI spreads fast,
   which Clark admitted sounds outlandish but also predicts “very disruptive”
   job impacts.
   -

   The world’s 10M scientists may soon direct “a billion virtual
   scientists,” Clark said while urging nations to build labs and robots
   before they run short.
   -

   He also said CEO Dario Amodei has floated limits on AI’s “ceiling of
   intelligence,” adding that he believes there is only “a small number of
   years” to act.

*Why it matters: *With the number of AI math and science breakthroughs in
the last few months alone, 2026 has handed Clark plenty of evidence.
Singularity talk used to live strictly in science fiction, and now one of
the people building it is saying it out loud to the folks who run the
global economy.

📈 *AI adoption has outpaced strategy
*


*The Rundown:* Atlassian’s 2026 State of the Developer Experience report,
based on global research with 1,560 respondents including devs and
engineering leaders, maps out clear paths for leaders to help their teams
manage the speed vs. friction tension happening right now.

*In the report, you’ll explore how:*

   -

   Devs are managing more output
   -

   An AI-native SDLC fixes bottlenecks
   -

   Only 23% of leaders have an AI strategy

Download the full State of DevEx 2026 Report today

AI & SECURITY
🔓 *One hacker’s AI agents break into 100+ companies
*

Image source: NorForge

*The Rundown: *Security firm NorForge revealed

that a Chinese-speaking hacker let AI agents do nearly all the work to
successfully break into the websites of 100+ companies, with Reuters
identifying victims like Cummins, Deere, and SharkNinja in the hack.

*The details:*

   -

   NorForge watched the attacks after finding 20+ hacker control panels for
   Cairn, an open-source tool for AI agents, left online with no password.
   -

   The hacker fed the agents a pre-screened list of busy online stores and
   orders under 100 Chinese characters, then sent them after over 1,200 sites.
   -

   NorForge puts AI costs near $50 per successful break-in, with a typical
   one taking nearly a day using Claude Code and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash.
   -

   It’s unclear if any data was taken, with SharkNinja calling the threat
   contained, Deere citing “remediation actions,” and Cummins “investigating.”

*Why it matters: *A month ago, we were writing

about “three guys with Claude” breaking into OpenAI, and now it’s one
hacker with an estimated $5K in tokens and a short note to their agents
hitting 100+ companies. AI’s offensive cyber capabilities are outpacing the
defensive ones, and a lot of companies are about to be caught in the
crosshairs.

AI TRAINING
🎙️ *Try ChatGPT’s new voices with GPT-Live-1.1
*

*The Rundown:* In this guide, you’ll try ChatGPT’s new voices, compare them
with the same short passage, and check whether a spoken correction reaches
the final answer.

*Step-by-step:*

   1.

   Open ChatGPT’s Voice settings and choose Live where available. Pick a
   voice and start a new chat with the guide’s fictional workshop notice
   2.

   Ask it to read the notice, then try the same words with another voice.
   Keep the language and instructions fixed so the comparison stays useful
   3.

   Try a regional voice in a language you know well. Listen for clear
   names, dates, and numbers, and ask for a slower repeat when needed
   4.

   Interrupt the notice with a new date and headcount. Check that those
   details change while the time and budget stay fixed
   5.

   Ask Voice to search OpenAI’s release notes. Open its source link and
   check the answer rather than trusting the spoken search cue alone

*Pro tip:* A new voice and a new model are different changes. Comparing
Bubbie with your usual voice does not prove a gain over GPT-Live-1. Pro
members get the practice prompts and listening checklist.

INCEPTION
⚡️ *Inception’s Mercury 3 speeds past rivals
*

Image source: Inception

*The Rundown: *AI startup Inception just launched

Mercury 3, a “diffusion” language model it says matches or beats OpenAI’s
GPT-6 Luna and Anthropic’s Claude Haiku 5.5 by its own numbers at 4-8x
their speed.

*The details: *

   -

   Language models write one at a time, while diffusion models draft many
   words at once and refine them, leading to outputs of 1,000+ tokens a
   second.
   -

   Inception pitches it as useful for apps where any lag shows, with early
   users running live tutors, voice customer support, and web-browsing agents
   on it.
   -

   Mercury 3 is priced at $0.20/$0.70 per million tokens, with the company
   saying the model is 40x the size of Mercury 1 while still maintaining the
   same speeds.
   -

   Co-founder Stefano Ermon said scaling diffusion is limited by “compute
   and data, not fundamental algorithmic barriers,” and a successor is already
   in training.

*Why it matters: *Mercury 3 won’t replace the frontier AI people use for
hard reasoning, and Inception isn’t pretending it will. But with OpenAI’s
Cerebras partnership and a new Ultrafast tier that pushes GPT-6 Astra as
high as 300 tokens/s, speed is clearly the next battleground — and
Inception is betting an alternative model type can win it.

*QUICK HITS*

COMMUNITY AI WORKFLOW OF THE DAY

▸ *A reader built a voice-enabled task management system with Claude*

*Today’s workflow comes from an anonymous Rundown reader:*

I’m 78, and I run a homestead, a home server, and a senior center, with
dozens of jobs underway at once. Most jobs get done a piece at a time,
while to-do apps only track whether something is “done” or “not done.”

So I built Taskmaster: a plain-text ledger inside a Claude Project. I first
tried building a large custom app, then scrapped it. One of my own rules
is, “Build the ugly version first.”

In the field, I speak notes into the Claude app on my phone. Claude saves
my exact words, updates each job’s progress, and asks me one question at a
time when something is unclear. When I ask, “What’s next?” it considers
deadlines, weather, and my energy level, then gives me one to three things
to do.

Anything tied to a specific time goes on my Google Calendar. Home Assistant
then reads the reminder aloud through my hearing aids. Today, it checked
the forecast and scheduled my paint job for the one day this week that
stays above 50°F overnight. The machine carries the complexity, so I don’t
have to.

*See the workflow on our Community Workflow Hub
*
